doc.title: Bill Goodwin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 28, 2025

title: Working with Joe Williams and the offer from Copenhagen
summary: A few weeks in the 1960s with Williams's trio, and an inquiry from Kenny Drew via Red Mitchell.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Joe Williams: the singer with Basie

blocks.x: Another beautiful person. I got to work with him for a few weeks in the ‘60s and he wanted a trio with Jim Hughart and Mike Melvoin and I and we went up to Seattle and played and did some radio up there which was later released as half of an LP. But anyway Joe loved the trio and we loved him. He was so great once we settled in together after a few nights man I just felt like going home every night. And he was so great that he — I would see him after that and he would always tell people that he really loved my playing and that I’d play things in his charts that weren’t written in there that he had written in there because he liked them so much. You know just little things. You know question and answer type stuff. But man what a beautiful cat, and what a great artist. So much fun to play with him. And it, you know like a lot of great people sharing also with this magnificent artist. I played, you know I loved playing with him and I would have stayed with him if Gary hadn’t called, except I had gotten an inquiry from Kenny Drew in Copenhagen but — through Red Mitchell about me coming there to play with him and Neils-Pederson. So I had these two — you know what should I do? Move to New York? Go to Copenhagen? Well I’d never been to Europe at that point though Red had already moved, Mitchell, and that’s why he recommended me. And so I took, and I always wanted to move to New York. New York, if you were in L.A. you knew about New York, play the big game, get validated. I got over that pretty quick. But I don’t regret it. Don’t regret it at all.
